fieldDescription: Adds an Optimal entry to the autofit goals of every ship in the refit screen. Other goals keep the game's own autofit.

fieldName: Fit for each ship's fleet role
fieldDescription: Each ship is built for its job in a fleet, from its designation and numbers: skirmisher frigates, flankers, line cruisers, capital anchors, carriers, battle carriers, support, phase, missile boats. The role sets who it mostly fights, firepower against staying alive, speed, range, point defense and fighters. Off: every ship is built as a generic duelist.

fieldName: Civilian ships: fit for the campaign
fieldDescription: Freighters, tankers, liners, salvage and survey ships never fight: no weapons, and campaign hullmods instead (cargo, fuel or berths by ship type, then burn speed, sensor profile, sensors, survey and salvage gear, treasure hunting, supply use). No vents or capacitors. Needs a spaceport to add them.

fieldName: Civilian ships: build in fleet-wide hullmods
fieldDescription: With Build in s-mods ticked, civilian ships that stay in the fleet for good (cruisers and capitals like the Atlas and Prometheus, and salvage rigs) build in the hullmods that help the whole fleet: Treasure Hunt Package, Surveying Equipment, High Resolution Sensors, then burn speed. Works in a single refit and in Optimize fleet; story points are spent only on Confirm. Built-in ones don't count against the logistics limit, so cargo, fuel or berths still fit.

Optimal looks at the rest of your fleet: fighter roles already covered (fighters, bombers, interceptors, support) and duplicate wings count for less, and with the Auto or Balanced style each ship leans toward the damage the fleet is short of (anti-shield or anti-armor). The fleet as a whole becomes the all-rounder. Optimize fleet balances every ship against the plan for the others; a single Optimal fit against the fleet as it stands.

secondaryValue: Auto, Balanced, Anti-shield, Anti-armor, Hull killer
fieldDescription: Auto picks per ship from its slots and role. Balanced covers all three layers: breaks shields, strips armor, kills hull. The others put most firepower into one layer and keep enough of the rest to finish the job.
Also adds Optimal (Balanced), (Anti-shield), (Anti-armor) and (Hull killer) goals, so each ship can use a different style.
Auto follows the ship (speed, armor, slot arcs). Long keeps every gun near the longest range; Close favours damage over range.
How long a typical engagement lasts. Short fights favour burst damage and missiles; long ones favour flux-efficient sustained fire.
Counts scripted effects (EMP arcs, shield-piercing, damage over time, chain hits) on top of the plain numbers, so rare weapons win when they really are stronger.
Gives rarer weapons (lower drop rate, higher tier, rare blueprints) a bonus on top of their measured strength. Off: weapons win only on measured strength, special effects included.

fieldName: Use items you can only get with cheats
fieldDescription: Off: weapons and LPCs with no blueprint, that no NPC faction knows and no ship in any mod carries (console allweapons gear like Yunru's gyrojets) are left out of fits, Optimize fleet and fleet orders. Omega, Threat and Dweller gear always counts.

On: when two weapons score about the same, the one the community rates higher for AI ships wins (Grievous69's 0.98a tier lists: Burst PD over LR PD, HVD over Gauss). It moves a weapon's value by about 5%% at most. Vanilla weapons only; other mods can add rows to data/config/jao_weapon_tiers.csv.
How much the rarest weapon gains when Prefer rare weapons is on (0.15 = +15%%), scaled down for less rare ones.
Weapons and fighters marked as priority in your faction doctrine win when they score within 1%% of the best other choice for a mount. The game's own refit autofit ignores those marks.

A weapon or LPC from a market must make the ship this much stronger for every 10,000 credits it costs, over what you own (0.01 = 1%% per 10,000 credits). Survival mode prices weapons x10 and LPCs x5. 0 ignores prices. Optimize fleet and Order fleet weapons buy nothing from markets.
Minimum point defense relative to the ship's size (1 = enough to stop a typical missile volley; 0 = none required).
Weapon ids or patterns, separated by commas (stardust_* skips every Stardust Ventures weapon). The Optimal fit never picks them.

Off: only hullmods that make nothing about the ship worse (no lost range, speed, handling, shield or flux; no higher supply, recovery, deployment, crew or crew salary cost; no s-mod penalty). On: drawbacks are weighed against the gains in battle (supply, deployment and salary costs aren't scored). Safety Overrides needs this on.

secondaryValue: Never, Frigates and destroyers, When it scores best
fieldDescription: Safety Overrides doubles dissipation but cuts range past 450, peak time by two thirds and stops venting. On 0.98.5a it also adds crew losses by peak time used and doubles the ship's crew salary. Frigates and destroyers: only on those, and only when it really scores best (short-range guns). When it scores best: any hull the game allows.
Off: never adds hullmods that only help in the campaign (cargo, fuel, sensors, burn).
Most new s-mods one Optimal fit or one Optimize fleet builds into one ship when the autofit box "Build in s-mods" is ticked, within the ship's own s-mod limit.
Most story points one Optimize fleet spends in total, biggest ships first. Story points to keep still applies.
An s-mod must make the ship at least this much stronger to be worth a story point (0.02 = 2%%).

When a clearly better set needs hullmods you don't know yet or can only fit at a spaceport, keep the slots those would take open; the other slots still get the best you have. The log says what's held.

fieldName: How much better to wait for
fieldDescription: Wait only when the best possible s-mods are at least this much better than the best you have now (0.1 = 10%%).

fieldName: Most days to hold a slot
fieldDescription: After this many days of holding s-mod slots for a missing hullmod, a ship builds the best you have in them.
Never spend story points below this many.

A button on the refit screen (also in LunaLib's refit menu) that plans every fleet ship's Optimal fit with all the weapon and fighter blueprints you know, lists what custom production would have to build, and queues it when you press Queue all.

Share of your credits one fleet order may cost (0.5 = half). The order is always the whole fleet's plan; what doesn't fit the budget (smaller ships last) is ordered the next time you press the button.
Random Assortment of Things: a Frontiers settlement with Ordnance Manufacturing takes the biggest ships' items up to its budget, at its prices, paid when ordered. The rest goes to custom production.
Writes each Optimal fit's scores and reasons to starsector.log.

fieldName: Debug: remove all s-mods and refund story points
fieldDescription: Turn on during a game and save the settings: every ship in your fleet loses its s-mods, built-in hullmods lose their s-mod bonus, and you get one story point back per s-mod. Bonus XP from building them is kept. Runs once each time it is turned on. Turn it off afterwards.
